results.title: Parsing Gigabytes of JSON per Second (Langdale & Lemire, 2019)
results.key_takeaway: First standard-compliant JSON parser to process GB/s on single core. Uses SIMD structural character classification in 64-byte blocks, producing bitmasks. Two-stage architecture: Stage 1 indexes structural characters, Stage 2 materializes values. Uses carry-less multiplication (CLMUL) for string region detection.

results.title: simdzone - SIMD DNS zone file parser inspired by simdjson
results.key_takeaway: Applies simdjson's SIMD structural indexing to DNS zone file parsing. Demonstrates the technique transfers well to non-JSON delimited formats. Uses vectorized classification and binary logic for string/sequence identification.

results.title: On-Demand JSON: A Better Way to Parse Documents? (Keiser & Lemire)
results.key_takeaway: Novel lazy/on-demand JSON parsing interface that materializes results only when accessed. Builds on simdjson's structural indexing but avoids full DOM construction. Relevant to our two-phase approach where Phase 1 indexes and Phase 2 materializes selectively.

results.title: simdjson Stage 1 structural indexer source code
results.key_takeaway: Reference implementation of SIMD structural indexing. Uses buf_block_reader for 64-byte block processing, json_string_scanner for quote state, json_scanner for structural character classification. Key pattern: classify -> string_scan -> structural_index.

results.title: Parsing Millions of DNS Records per Second (Koekkoek & Lemire, 2024)
results.key_takeaway: simdzone uses SIMD data parallelism for DNS zone file parsing. Achieves millions of records/sec. Shows that SIMD structural character detection generalizes beyond JSON to other text formats with quote/escape semantics.

queries.query: SIMD CSV parsing high performance vectorized delimiter detection

results.title: Fast CSV processing with SIMD (Chris Wellons, 2021)
results.key_takeaway: Implements csvquote using SIMD. Uses CLMUL-based quote pairing to transform quote bitmask into quoted-region mask. Order-of-magnitude speedup over naive approach. Key technique: multiply quote bitmask by -1 using carry-less multiply to get prefix-XOR.

results.title: geofflangdale/simdcsv - SIMD CSV parser (C++)
results.key_takeaway: By simdjson co-author Geoff Langdale. Applies simdjson's exact approach to CSV: vectorized classification for comma/quote/newline, CLMUL for quote-state tracking, bitmask extraction for field boundaries. Reference implementation for our approach.

results.title: friendlymatthew/simdcsv - Rust SIMD CSV parser
results.key_takeaway: Rust implementation using PCLMULQDQ for quote pairing and vqtbl1q_u8 (NEON) for vectorized classification. Processes 64 bytes at a time. Adheres to RFC 4180. Demonstrates cross-platform SIMD approach (x86 + ARM).

results.title: medialab/simd-csv - Specialized Rust CSV readers/writers leveraging SIMD
results.key_takeaway: Active Rust crate (4000+ downloads) using SIMD for CSV parsing. Recent (2025-2026). Uses memchr for SIMD-accelerated character search as foundation.

results.title: cisv - 'Fastest CSV Parser Ever Made' (2025)
results.key_takeaway: C implementation using branchless programming and SIMD. Eliminates branch mispredictions through lookup tables and conditional moves. Achieves high throughput by avoiding if/switch in hot path.

results.title: fastcsv - Rust SIMD CSV parser based on simdcsv
results.key_takeaway: RFC 4180 compliant. Uses AVX2 on x86-64, NEON on ARM. Migrated from C++ to Rust. Demonstrates viability of SIMD CSV parsing in safe language.

queries.query: vectorized text parsing branchless finite automaton bitmask

results.title: SMH: Shuffle-based Matching Sequences (Geoff Langdale, 2018)
results.key_takeaway: PSHUFB-based matching technique from Hyperscan. Uses shuffle instruction as lookup table for character classification. Core pattern: PSHUFB + PAND + comparison chain. Applies to any character class detection in SIMD.

results.title: Regular Expression Matching using Bit Vector Automata (Le Glaunec et al.)
results.key_takeaway: Uses bit-vector representations for NFA state sets. SIMD-friendly approach to regex matching. Relevant technique: representing automaton states as bitmasks and advancing via bitwise operations.

results.title: Recognizing string prefixes with SIMD (Lemire, 2023)
results.key_takeaway: Demonstrates SIMD techniques for string classification tasks. Shows how to use SIMD comparison instructions for multi-pattern matching.

queries.query: RFC 4180 CSV parser benchmark comparison arrow-csv xsv pandas throughput

results.title: Julia CSV Reader Benchmarks: 10-20x faster than Python
results.key_takeaway: Julia's CSV.jl achieves 10-20x speedup over Python/R through multi-threaded parsing and type inference. Establishes that large speedups over pandas are achievable with better algorithms.

results.title: SmarterCSV 1.15.2 benchmarks (2026)
results.key_takeaway: Ruby CSV parser using C backend. Benchmarks against zsv (SIMD C CSV parser). Shows that end-to-end pipeline optimization matters as much as raw parsing speed.

results.title: bench_csv - CSV processing benchmarks for different technologies
results.key_takeaway: Benchmark suite comparing CSV parsers across languages/frameworks. Useful reference for our benchmarking methodology.

queries.query: speculative execution in parsers parallel parsing quote state prediction

results.title: Speculative Distributed CSV Data Parsing for Big Data Analytics (Ge et al., SIGMOD 2019)
results.key_takeaway: KEY PAPER. Proposes speculation-based approach for parallel CSV parsing. Each chunk speculatively assumes quote-state context. Validates on 11,000+ real-world datasets. Shows speculation rarely fails due to statistical properties of CSV. Directly relevant to our item_016 parallel design.

results.title: Parallel Speculative DOM-based XML Parser (IEEE)
results.key_takeaway: Applies speculative parallelism to XML parsing. Chunks are parsed independently with speculative context; misspeculations trigger re-parsing. Analogous approach to our CSV parallel parsing design.

results.title: Parallel parsing made practical (ScienceDirect, 2015)
results.key_takeaway: Theoretical framework for parallel parsing of operator-precedence grammars. PAPAGENO toolchain. Shows that text can be split into chunks with speculative state resolution at boundaries.

results.title: PostgreSQL: Speed up COPY FROM text/CSV parsing using SIMD (pgsql-hackers, 2025)
results.key_takeaway: Active PostgreSQL development effort to add SIMD-accelerated CSV parsing to COPY FROM. Shows industry adoption of SIMD CSV parsing techniques. Uses similar approach to our structural character detection.

queries.query: PCLMULQDQ carry-less multiplication prefix XOR quote parity CSV parser

results.title: Geoff Langdale email on PCLMULQDQ for quote pairing
results.key_takeaway: Langdale describes inventing the CLMUL quote-pairing trick for simdjson. Multiplying quote bitmask by -1 via carry-less multiply transforms quote positions into quoted-region mask. ARM equivalent: PMULL. Key insight: this is prefix-XOR computed in hardware.

results.title: Intel PCLMULQDQ specification and GCM mode usage
results.key_takeaway: Intel's official documentation on carry-less multiplication. Originally designed for AES-GCM crypto. Repurposed for parsing by simdjson team. Available on all modern x86-64 processors since Westmere (2010).

results.title: friendlymatthew/simdcsv - uses PCLMULQDQ for CSV quote pairing
results.key_takeaway: Practical Rust implementation demonstrating PCLMULQDQ for CSV quote-state computation. Includes both x86 and ARM paths. Shows the technique works correctly for RFC 4180 quoted fields with embedded delimiters.
